scope: Player task ergonomics: proximity, visible dependencies, scrolling, return paths and local feedback

objectMoveDistance.unit: screen pixels from selected miniature centre to Move button centre, same 1280x720 viewport; initial action was also offscreen

realTaskScenarios: Guest and room settings form a returnable task without searching or scrolling
Buying an adventure keeps its originating table available
Contextual object actions remain adjacent during camera changes and commit a real rotation
Equipment supplies and local result are reachable from the selected device
Destructive decisions stay in their subject card and cancellation changes nothing
Start still executes directly, reports finish and room choices survive reload
limitations: Scripted real-browser journeys plus visual inspection; no novice-participant study or physical touchscreen test.
The results apply to measured tasks and layouts, not a guarantee that every possible future interface state is convenient.
Catalogue browsing, long histories and advanced options may scroll; primary task actions remain available.
